gaps.sentence: 'We're moving to Lisbon,' they announced. They announced that they ___ to Lisbon.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous backshifts to past continuous: are moving → were moving.

gaps.sentence: 'I'll have finished by noon,' she promised. She promised she ___ finished by noon.
gaps.explanation: will have + past participle becomes would have + past participle.

gaps.sentence: 'I had already eaten,' she said. She said she ___ already eaten.
gaps.explanation: The past perfect cannot backshift further; it remains had + past participle.

gaps.sentence: They ___ breaking the window, but nobody believed them.
gaps.explanation: Deny + -ing reports a rejection of the accusation; 'but nobody believed them' confirms the meaning.

gaps.sentence: 'Please don't smoke in here,' the host said. The host asked me ___ in there.
gaps.explanation: Negative requests: asked me not to smoke; 'here' shifts to 'there'.

gaps.sentence: "I will call you tomorrow." — She said she ___ me the next day.
"Can you help me?" — She asked ___ help her.
'It was me who ate the last biscuit,' the boy admitted. The boy ___ eating the last biscuit.
gaps.explanation: Admit takes a gerund (admit doing) or admit that + clause — never admit to do.
